query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor concentration of aluminum (e.g., ~1–2 at.%) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will enable the formation of a continuous, protective Al2O3 layer upon exposure to high-temperature oxidizing environments, thereby significantly improving its oxygen resistance without adversely affecting its room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr with known ductility (8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility) and high-temperature yield strength (163–530 MPa at 1000 °C, strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹), but with inadequate inherent oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled addition of aluminum (approximately 1–2 atomic percent) into the alloy composition during casting.
generation.conditions: Exposure at 800 °C in air for 5 hours, as used in previous oxidation-protection studies, with mechanical loading conditions maintained (if applicable) at similar strain rate boundaries (i.e., 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹) to ensure performance preservation.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, adherent Al2O3 (alumina) layer on the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: The added Al preferentially oxidizes to form a dense alumina scale that acts as an oxygen barrier. This protective oxide layer slows further oxygen ingress and mitigates pesting, thereby enhancing the oxidation resistance without substantially altering the alloy’s intrinsic mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-modified alloy will show a reduced oxidation rate, evidenced by lower weight gain and preserved structural integrity (i.e., absence of pesting) after exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
generation.baseline: The untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibiting inadequate oxygen resistance under identical high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
generation.boundary: Testing is limited to the 800 °C, 5-hour air exposure environment (with secondary mechanical performance verification at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹, as per the performance constraints).
generation.uncertainty: The precise aluminum concentration required to optimize oxide scale formation while fully preserving the mechanical performance is not established and may require further calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of the alloy: one as the standard equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr (control) and the other with 1–2 at.% added Al (intervention). Both sets should be processed using identical casting and heat-treatment parameters. Expose samples from each batch to air at 800 °C for 5 hours. Post-exposure, evaluate surface oxide structure via microscopy and measure weight gain (as an indicator of oxidation kinetics). Additionally, perform mechanical tests at room temperature and high temperature (e.g., at 1000 °C, strain rates between 10⁻⁴ and 10⁻² s⁻¹) to assess the retention of ductility and yield strength.
measurements: Weight gain after 5 h oxidation at 800 °C
Surface oxide scale continuity and composition (e.g., via SEM/EDS or XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-modified alloy does not exhibit a significantly lower weight gain and/or fails to develop a continuous, protective Al2O3 scale compared to the untreated control, or if its mechanical properties degrade relative to the baseline, then the hypothesis supporting improved oxygen resistance via Al addition is falsified.
